connection: Per-request sqlite3 connection opened via db.connect() and always closed in a finally block.
queries: SELECT-only queries against the movies table: full published catalog ordered by year DESC, genre-filtered browse ordered by rating DESC, and single-movie detail by id.
transactions: None. All catalog reads are single queries with no transaction boundaries.
n_plus_one: None. Each handler runs exactly one query; no per-row queries.
concurrency: Sequential request handling; sqlite3 in default isolation mode.
orm: No ORM. Raw sqlite3 with named row access (sqlite3.Row).

optimization_targets.description: The format_movie and format_movies helpers are defined inline in main.py. Move them to a dedicated catalog.py module so they can be reused elsewhere and keep main.py focused on HTTP concerns.
New module that receives the format_movie and format_movies helpers exactly as they appear in main.py. No logic, formatting, or return shape is modified — only the file they live in changes.

notes: Only the two formatting helpers are extracted — they are pure data formatting functions that map sqlite3 rows to dicts. db.py is untouched. All handlers produce byte-identical responses.
